findings.title: Data race on init counter
findings.body: In searchSupport.init the errgroup goroutines each execute totalBatchesIndexed++ on a plain int captured from the outer scope. With initWorkers > 1 this is a concurrent read-modify-write without atomic or mutex, so it is a data race and the reported namespaced_indexed count is unreliable.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
findings.body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no cacheMu held, while BuildIndex concurrently does b.cache[key]=idx under lock and GetIndex uses RLock. Concurrent map read and write in Go is a fatal error / race. After removing the coarse BuildIndex lock, concurrent builds during startup make this reachable, and searchSupport.init calls TotalDocs after concurrent builds.

findings.title: Concurrent duplicate BuildIndex for same key corrupts file index
findings.body: Removing the global cacheMu around BuildIndex leaves only a short lock for the final map store. Two goroutines for the same NamespacedResource can both miss GetIndex, both call bleve.New on the same directory path and both build, then last-writer-wins in the map. Concurrent bleve.New on the same dir can fail or leave a partially written index, wastes work, double-increments IndexTenants, and leaks the loser index.

findings.title: Watch loop never ends and panics on closed channel
findings.body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background, starts WatchWriteEvents, then loops as for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } with no ok check and no cancellation tied to server Stop. When the backend poller stops it closes the channel, the receive returns nil, and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type causing a nil panic. The goroutine also leaks after Stop because it does not watch any done context.

findings.title: handleEvent dereferences IndexMetrics without nil check
findings.body: searchSupport.init guards IndexMetrics with if IndexMetrics != nil, implying it can be nil, but handleEvent calls IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds.WithLabelValues(...).Inc/Dec and IndexMetrics.IndexLatency...Observe unconditionally. Any deployment or test with nil metrics will panic on the first watch event.

findings.title: Stop no longer gates RPCs after lazy Init removal
findings.body: server.Stop sets initErr to stopping/stopped, which previously caused all later RPCs to fail via their s.Init(ctx) check using sync.Once state. The PR removes all those checks, so after Stop the server keeps serving Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/Blobs. It also makes NewResourceServer block on full index build and fail construction where callers previously expected lazy initialization, and leaks the background cancel func when Init fails.

findings.title: Postgres storage-server test disabled
findings.body: The integration test for the storage-server target now skips postgres entirely. Since this PR changes startup initialization ordering that is backend-sensitive, losing postgres coverage hides regressions the test was meant to catch.
